title: Repetition periods of class 3 rules grow rapidly with system size

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Repetition periods of class 3 rules grow rapidly with system size

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In cellular automata on a finite cyclic lattice, a rapid increase of repetition period with lattice size is characteristic of class 3 behavior, with large fluctuations as size changes; among elementary rules only rule 45 appears to give periods always near the maximum possible.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In general, a rapid increase with size is characteristic of class 3 behavior. Of the elementary rules, however, only rule 45 seems to yield periods that always stay close to the maximum of 2^n.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Systems of Limited Size and Class 2 Behavior” (from p. 255), p. 258. Scope: elementary cellular automata on cyclic lattices of size n

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Exact period computation is straightforward for moderate sizes and public sequence resources aid replication. The asymptotic and uniqueness components require proof or much broader enumeration than standard analyses provide.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate cyclic lattices across increasing n for every elementary rule and specified initial-state sampling, compute transient and cycle lengths, and compare growth rates and fluctuations by class. Search explicitly for rules besides 45 whose periods remain near 2^n over the tested range.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Finite n cannot prove an all-n statement about rule 45.

“Characteristic” and “near maximum” need thresholds.

The initial-state convention affects measured periods.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Period versus ring size is an exact computation, and the single-black-cell protocol is the one in the figure captions, so moderate n for all 256 elementary rules is a fair small-team project. The distinctive clause is that only rule 45 stays close to 2^n for every n, and a table up to n near 30 cannot close every n. The class 3 growth contrast is visible in the same tables as a restricted-scope result.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On a ring of size n, start each elementary rule from a single black cell, detect the cycle, and compare its length with 2^n. Rule 45 staying nearer that ceiling than every other elementary rule, with class 3 periods rising much faster than class 2 periods, would support the claim over the computed range.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Always, for every n, is not settled by any finite table.

Cycles near 2^n at n around 30 cost on the order of a billion steps per orbit.

The curves use one black cell, a special orbit rather than the longest cycle in the state space.
